query: Why do some agents have longer resolution times?

per_column.name: assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: The query asks why some AGENTS have longer resolution times; the agent identity is the candidate cause whose effect on the outcome is being attributed. It is the treatment, explicitly named in the query.

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Incident type plausibly affects resolution time (some categories are harder) and can also correlate with which agents get assigned (specialization routing), making it a common cause of both treatment and outcome. Not named in query.

per_column.name: problem_scope
per_column.rationale: The breadth of a problem (facility-wide vs individual device) drives longer resolution and may influence agent assignment (senior agents get bigger scope). Plausible common cause, not named in query.

per_column.name: incident_complexity_signal
per_column.rationale: Intrinsic complexity raises resolution time and can steer assignment toward particular agents; a plausible common cause. Not named in query. (Some risk it overlaps with a mediator of scope, but as an assignment-driving pre-treatment trait it functions as a confounder.)

per_column.name: agent_closure_alignment
per_column.rationale: Whether the closing agent matches the assigned agent is an outcome of the resolution process (handoffs occur during/after resolution). It is downstream of both agent and resolution, so it is a post-treatment collider/mediator, not a confounder; adjusting for it would introduce bias.

judge.rationale: The system supplies a clear treatment (assigned_agent, the cause under attribution) plus three variables not named in the query that plausibly cause both agent assignment (via routing/specialization) and resolution time, realising the causal-attribution setup. The confounders were surfaced from the data rather than copied from the query. One added column (agent_closure_alignment) is a post-treatment collider/mediator and should not be adjusted for, lowering overall quality; complexity and scope also carry some overlap risk. Overall a genuine but imperfect causal-estimation scaffold.
